steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: This... isn't possible.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: If true, then this whole time, the Abyssal Hunters have been looking for something right under their noses.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What that possibility signifies is too vile to put into words.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: From beginning to end, the Eye of Iberia has always born witness to the aftermath of calamity. But it is just a sinking eyeball, unable to speak.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...What does this mean?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It means Ægir's demise is accelerating.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It means that... if even cities at this distance are sending out distress signals, then the Stultifera Navis has been circling above their nest since the very beginning.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...The Hunters are all in danger.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I know what you're thinking, but we have only one ship and the two of us.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Saving the Stultifera was not realistic.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You may not mind a few Abyssal Hunters dying at sea, but what we would be strangling in its cradle is opportunity. For both Ægir and Iberia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dario died a warrior's death. Wouldn't you want to gain some valuable knowledge from the mouth of the surviving Inquisitor?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is our last chance.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: No. A powerless city, almost reduced to ruins. How many Ægir have already fallen to the ocean?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We must act cautiously, or we will be leaping into the flames.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even so, this is our last chance.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If we wait until Ægir can no longer respond, until another Silence has fallen over Iberia, then indeed, the true enemy will appear.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But at that point, would it matter?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I understand you have your responsibilities. You don't want to take any risks until the Penal Battalion has full control over this place.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So I'll go alone.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...I know better than to underestimate the power of you and your pet, but it's a long trip. Are you sure you'll make it on your own?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Hunters bleed a special kind of blood. Sea Terrors aren't necessarily that hostile towards ordinary ships.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I can only hope you didn't just make that up to assuage my fears.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's not a lie I would have come up with anyway. Regardless, I can't leave the Hunters behind.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You'd better bring back the Hunters and Irene, Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Ah, um...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, survey our surroundings. If those Sea Terrors went back into hiding underwater, don't rile them up.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We need time, since the ship's taken some damage from the trip.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Answers with a nod)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: This ship...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The one the Hunters took was left by the Inquisition's spies.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lord Carmen's original plan was to join up with the Penal Battalion at Gran Faro, establish a frontline headquarters, and push forward on a medium-sized naval vessel.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So, this lone boat, abandoned on the shores of Gran Faro, is our final hope.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I can help... I'll go take a look at the boat. I've never actually repaired a ship before, but I do have some tools with me.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um, can you really head out to sea on something like this?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you don't think so, then probably not— Wait!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Out of the way, Jordi!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Woah, huh?!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: S-Sea Terrors?!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Waaaaah—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They were hiding in the shadow of the reef? Mon3tr!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Screeches excitedly)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Jordi! Get off the boat!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I, I can't, something's pushing on it! The anchor's gone!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'll try to steer it back—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Jump off! The Sea Terrors are swarming around it!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, go rescue him.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wait, wait— Then we'd lose the boat then! I, I'll try to steer it back! Urgh!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Watch out behind you!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Save Jordi first.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Cheers in response)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Whirlpools, changing currents, and the Sea Terrors are unusually active again... What's going on here?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Stretches out claws)

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: You want me to grab on and fly back with you? But, then the boat will— Woah?!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Screeches urgently)
Jordi knows that if doesn't take this opportunity, then he'll drift into the endless ocean along with the ship.
There's no other choice. He has to return to the Eye of Iberia and hide inside the lighthouse.
Just like he hid in that little town for over a decade.
Just like he hid when Dario died.
Just like with Thiago.
He clings to the mast to avoid falling into the aberrant waves. Mon3tr is visibly dissatisfied, urging him on.
Sea Terrors leap from the water's surface from time to time, darting back and forth rapidly and kicking up plumes of water. The Eye of Iberia is already becoming smaller and smaller.
He sees words carved crookedly into the boat's mast:
'Gran Faro'

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...I will go in Kal'tsit's place.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: All I have to do is... find that ship, and bring everyone back, right? That doesn't sound too hard...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Compared to losing the ship and waiting helplessly under the lighthouse... it's a gamble I have to take!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I can do this on my own!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: As long as even one of our kin touches upon the ultimate answer to life, we will be able to re-weave the laws of the cosmos from beginning to end.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Before we are given our next Revelation, we shall find a way.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Even if Ishar'mla refuses to answer. Even if our kind will never know the divine Will.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: We will still survive.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Shark.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Hmm.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Our kin have conveyed their will. Nutrients are sufficient. No longer must we feed on each other.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I should return to the nest. You should come with me.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Running away so soon?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: It barely took any damage, but the ship's in tatters.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You're still going on about that stuff, Amaia? Why don't just stay put and let me kill you like a good girl?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Our kind calls me back. They call for me to share my fruits with them.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I shall heed their call. When that is done, I shall heed your call. I shall seek you out, and you shall kill me.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Haha... Of course I can't let you leave. If I let you go, how many Seaborn just like you are going to end up all over the place?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Amaia sure knows how to make things hard for me. If only she were as simple and straightforward as Quintus.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: What a shame I couldn't keep her around with that dance.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You talk too much, scum!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ishar-mla. I've always wanted to meet you.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: What happened? Why doesn't He speak anymore? Where is He?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Pah... It's like hacking at water. No resistance at all.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Are you Him? Is He you?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I have no idea what you're talking about. If you mean that big guy, He's already dead.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Death. Withering. He exists beyond these concepts. His voice, by no means signifies the end of life.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What do your kind call Him? The same as those cultists? Your 'god' has already withered and fallen into the abyss.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: God?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: No. This is what we call Him—

a.text: The hardship we suffer is ever present.
The life we thirst for is ever present.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ishar-mla. Once more, I feel His pulse.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Kin. You swam together to His abode in the abyss, where even death drowns.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: We have lost contact with Him, but His choices can only lead to the future.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Kin, your information... Nay, the flow of your emotions.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You feel it, Ishar-mla. Because you have left the arid land and returned home.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Our blood flows in your veins. His blood flows in your veins. You are Him.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I am the Abyssal Hunter, Skadi.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: No matter. As you say, thus you are. Abyssal Hunter, Ska-di.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ishar-mla, we await His answer. Be it on the other end of time, He will answer us.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Until then, until our answer finally comes—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: —We many shall live on.
Gladiia silently appears behind the Seaborn, the lance in her hand actually puncturing the creature's body.
It is followed immediately by the cacophony of a whirling chainsaw.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Too slow. You're becoming weak, so just accept getting turned into paste.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Nngh—!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: —Too shallow, it's not good enough! Ugh!
The heat of the sweltering flames sweeps down the long corridor. The Stultifera is groaning.
The Seaborn does not attack the vulnerable Skadi.
It simply stares at her in silence. A very strange sensation. Just like at Sal Viento.
It is 'watching' her, Skadi thinks.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Ugh, the ship is... at its limit. It'll start sinking very soon.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It's trying to get away! Argh!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Below you!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Don't move, monster.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I won't allow you to return to the sea.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You are pitifully weak, human. Even as nutrition, you are not enough to nourish our kin.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Now that nutrients are plentiful, we require only time.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: This place is far from your territory. You have no reason to interfere with us.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You and your kind cannot be judged by the law. I don't think I have any means of eradicating you for Iberia either.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Law? Burdensome rules of survival, as Amaia once said.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Compared to our kin, you are indeed too weak.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —But I will not let you escape, ocean scum.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: This is the last shot.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: And sure enough, I can't even... *cough*... leave a scar on you...

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Emotional. How strange, human. You are so weak, driven by emotions, trying to escape my hunger.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Escape, yes. Escape. Fear? But why do you still stand here then? Why do you attack me? Why... do you not flee from me?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Do you... also wish to make a contribution to 'we many'?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Who gave you the right to interrogate me?
The Seaborn no longer speaks. The creature before it is not kin.
Predation does not require the tool called language.
But before it can strike, a shadow drops down from the darkness of the ceiling.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Alfonso?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Tch. Haven't seen the color of its blasted blood since it became like this.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: This hunt— *spit*. Is almost over. You killed my chief mate, and you WILL pay.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You both, paradoxical beings. You still refuse to become our kin.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You have eaten many of us. Yet you refuse to become part of us.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Make your choice. Not much time remains.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Hunt, acquire nutrients, return to we many.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Or, cease your bodily movements, give up the gift of life, and pass it on to our other kin.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Choose.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Irene.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Yes! Um, why are you calling my name, though?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Tell me, do you have a way to return to land?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But I must go back.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I can't stand against the Seaborn, but Iberia can. I'll carry this final warning with me. What happened to all of you, what Gladiia saw, I must bring all of it back.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: You're starting to sound like a Messenger.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...That's fine. I can be whatever I want.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But I must go back.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ngh?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: My ship is about to sink.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Sixty years. It's been over sixty years. But because of your arrival, we must now face the end.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Tell me.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: How does Iberia remember the great Captain Alfonso?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: 'Alfonso Under the Pomegranate Tree'. 'The Hero, Alfonso.' 'The Sunken Alfonso.'

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: There are many people... who held onto hope that the Stultifera never sank. But we weren't able to head out to sea.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: If... If you really are Lord Alfonso...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You have become a paragon to countless Iberian soldiers.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Hmph... Pomegranate tree, huh... How pretentious.
A flash of intense passion shimmers across the captain's eyes.
Since the dark clouds and turbulent waves trapped them inside this cage, few things have ever stirred his heart.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: It's gotten weaker.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I'll hold it back.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: E-Explosions?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I thought the Originium boilers got knocked out of commission a long time ago, but the impact just now seems to have ignited the engine.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: The flames will spread upward. I've always wondered how these things taste flame-grilled.
The heat makes the Seaborn uncomfortable.
It has become weak. Its kin are encircling it. It is unable to reach the sea.
It screams. But its calls are not answered.
No. Kin are coming. Closer. It can hear the voices of its kin.
They speak—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Die.
Gladiia does not hesitate. Skadi and Specter sever its body.
It tries to regenerate. It tries to break free. But this time, Alfonso clings to its body in a death grip.
He makes use of his already mutated arm.
It feels its lifeforce slipping away.
It sees Specter raise her weapon again.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Goodbye, Amaia.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Let's write off the debt this time.

steps.name: Sal Viento Bishop
steps.text: What? You want to talk to her again? What can that filth possibly say that's worth hearing?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You don't understand, Quintus.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: She told me about her life in Ægir.

steps.name: Sal Viento Bishop
steps.text: So what? If you want knowledge, a Herald can tell you far more.

steps.name: Sal Viento Bishop
steps.text: All we need to do is summon the Voice of the Deeps, and you will be able to obtain anything you want.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: That's why I said you don't understand, Quintus.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: What I want to deconstruct, to witness, to caress, to break... has never been those cities. On land or in water, it's all the same.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: I want to hear about their lives. About the wonderful lives they once had, about how they built their society, about how they defended their home.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: About how they cannibalized each other. About how they met their destruction, just like us.

steps.name: Sal Viento Bishop
steps.text: Like us?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The people who defile Ægir are Ægirs like you. The people who defile Iberia are Iberians like me.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Heh... The results of the experiment are already plain as day. If we still need more comparisons, she'll go mad and hate us.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: She'll hate us, and to be honest, I hate them too. Self-destructive soldiers. A self-righteous country. Falling into a self-inflicted trap.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: But sometimes... You have to admit that we're more like them, more like humans, than we are like Seaborn.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: We'll probably be fighting forever.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —It worked!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Hey, Captain Alfonso, are you alright?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Compared to my ship, not half bad.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Are you really dead, Amaia? It can't be that easy, can it?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Limbs twitch)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Don't waste your breath on it.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Convulsing) Lauren...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I'm here. I'm right here.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Seems like our positions are reversed now, Amaia.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Too bad for you, I've never... been one for science experiments. Not in the slightest.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Quivers with torn muscles)

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Go ahead and die, you inferior, evolution-crazed creature.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: And be forgotten.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...That should settle things.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Seaborn. Even more Seaborn are nearby. They're approaching.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: And this ship's about to go down.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Even when my consciousness was hazy, I was still aware of how much effort it took for us to get here. Seems like we'll be running up against another wall.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Did you get what you came for, Swordfish?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Ulpianus took it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: It's our fault that we failed to preserve the prototype technology on this ship, but...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: That doesn't mean we came here in vain.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Captain.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: It doesn't matter. Garcia already said that today's the last day of our voyage.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...For a long, long time, our will to survival has been slowly eaten away.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: At first, our greatest enemies were anxiety, suspicion, uncertainty, and fear. But later...

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Our emotions started drifting away from us. A longing for the ocean gnawed at our nerves, and one after another one, we forgot the glory of being a crewmember of the Stultifera Navis.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: I watched them jump into the sea one by one, or I beheaded them before they could. I admit... that was a bit extreme.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: This long nightmare of survival has finally come to an end.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Seawater is pouring into the ship. This whole place is being eaten by the nethersea brand.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Inquisitor, this technology here, these Originium boiler techniques, will they be useful to the current Iberia?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Everything on the Stultifera is a precious national treasure. Ever since the Profound Silence, Iberia has had a large amount of Islander technology that cannot be reproduced.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: And it's not just because we lost our fleet and our cities. Because of the judgment we passed on the Ægir, we lost so much of our talent too.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It was... necessary. Even now, I don't think that a soft-hearted strategy full of kindness could have combatted the Church of the Deep.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: If, today, we are forced to lose Stultifera Navis—the Ship of Fools—then I think... it would be a heavy blow, but it's something that was doomed to happen from the start.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Hmph, hogwash. The state religion's always been like this.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Ægirs.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Take care of the Iberian. She can't swim back.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...That I can promise you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The explosions are getting worse—this side's leaning!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We need to go, Skadi. Cut off a bit of the rafters above you!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Hurry! Irene!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I, I know! But what about Alfonso?!

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: How far will the currents take us? Or are we going to go around in circles? Isn't this place on top of their nest?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Regardless, looks like we're going to have to swim back.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: W-What?!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Go. Get the hell off of my ship, like I told you from the start.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Just go. I'll stay here. This is my Iberia, and the captain goes down with the ship.
Alfonso slowly lowers himself into the throne. He closes his eyes.
The warmth of the bright Iberian sun as it splashes at an angle across the deck.
The aroma of a winery. The melody of his hometown.
A damp and empty room. Freshly burgeoning petri dishes.
The ocean's waves.
The ocean he once knew. The warmth of Garcia's hand. Breogan's lonely countenance. Carmen's smile. His comrades' roars resonating through the sky.
He opens his eyes, and lets out a hearty laugh as everything is consumed by the flames.
His laughter crosses through time, until it reaches a small town of pomegranate flowers, where one can smell the sea upon the breeze, and mingles with the first cries of a newborn child.
Alfonso. That is what the people call him.
He lifts his old, rusty blade, and places it against his neck. He prays. He laughs.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Hah. What a joke! Remember this well, Irene! Return to land and sing the praises of Alfonso's feats!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: The last monster that Alfonso slew... was himself!
The ship breaks apart.
The glow of the flame blankets a sea that had been silent for nearly a hundred years.
An era comes to an end.
A legend passes into history.
In the distance, the sun rises.
Here sinks the Stultifera, and with it, the long-cherished wishes of Iberia, nay, of all civilization.
All succumbing to calamity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: I think I heard... a voice.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: No, it must be my old age. These things happen.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lord Carmen...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're crying?
Water?
Right...
The Stultifera... sank.
I'm in the ocean? The ocean... is a dangerous place.
It's dangerous, yes.
I have to return to Iberia!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Glub—! Gurgle—!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Stop trying to breathe like that. Underwater breathing is beyond you. Most Ægirs can't either.
I want to say something in return. But of course, I am underwater, and cannot.
Despite trying to contain my instincts, I can't help but clutch at her clothes like a helpless child.
But, I can see it.
The light reflected in her pupils.
It comes from the bottom of the sea.
Specter does not say anything, but I can feel her arms trembling slightly around me.
Maybe because of the battle we just fought? Maybe? Or, something to do with the light?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I'll bring you back up. Hang on tight.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —Glub!
My vision blurs.
So that's... what the bottom of the ocean... looks like.
Then—
—Is this Ægir?
The Seaborn quietly watches the distant flames disappearing beneath the waters.
The ship sinks into the ocean. Along with the flames. Along with everything.
Its kin answer its call. They all return to the many.
Surrounded by the many's embrace, it takes only a moment for the dying to be given new life.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ishar-mla. I will bring you all, back home.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: —Let's all, die together, with Alfonso.
The chief mate grips the Seaborn in its jaws and charges all the way into the seabed's murky darkness.
Its lover. Its memories. Its identity. As its charge slows, its consciousness dissolves into the ocean.
But still it bites down on the Seaborn.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: The waters, make you nostalgic. Swim, and you will awaken.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Accept it. You are one of we many. We have long awaited you.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: I am... Garcia... I am... Alfonso's...

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Then why did you stop swimming? Your signal is just like mine.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Your wounds have all healed. You are accepting who you are.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: No—!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Why no?
The Chief Mate's consciousness is blurring.
Is it biting down on this Seaborn? Or, is it leaping into the Seaborn's embrace, seeking its succor?
It... It is forced to accept.
The sea makes it very comfortable. The Seaborn's thoughts flood into its mind.
Is it Garcia, Chief Mate of the Stultifera?
No, it is a Seaborn. It is one of we many—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Glub... (sounds of bubbles being blown) Gurgle... (sounds of bubbles popping)

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You will die a human being, Garcia.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A step up from Amaia.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Ul...pianus... Kin...

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Thank... you...

Ulpianus watches the two sink to the bottom of the ocean, seemingly locked in an embrace beyond death. Like flowers growing side-by-side, they shrink, and wither. And beyond a certain depth, they are carried away by the undercurrent.
He does not lift his head until they are completely out of sight.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia, you must heed my warnings.
